questions.q: R-CH$_2$OH is converted into R-CHO by reacting with ______.
questions.explanation: PCC selectively oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without over-oxidising it to the carboxylic acid, unlike alkaline KMnO$_4$; LiAlH$_4$ and Na/C$_2$H$_5$OH are reducing agents, not oxidants.

questions.q: Glycerol is a trihydric alcohol. It contains ______.
options: One primary, one secondary and one tertiary alcoholic groups
Two primary and one secondary alcoholic groups
Two secondary and one primary alcoholic groups
One primary and two tertiary alcoholic groups
questions.explanation: Glycerol, CH$_2$OH-CHOH-CH$_2$OH, has two terminal primary -OH groups and one middle secondary -OH group.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of CH$_3$-C(CH$_3$)$_2$-O-C$_2$H$_5$ is
questions.explanation: The compound is (CH$_3$)$_3$C-O-C$_2$H$_5$; naming the longer chain (propane) with an ethoxy substituent at C2 gives 2-ethoxy-2-methylpropane.

questions.q: C$_4$H$_{10}$ undergoes: (i) (BH$_3$)$_2$ then H$_2$O$_2$/NaOH $\rightarrow$ P; (ii) P with CrO$_3$ (anhydrous medium) $\rightarrow$ Q; (iii) Q with CH$_3$MgBr then H$_3$O$^+$ $\rightarrow$ R + Mg(OH)Br. The organic compounds P, Q and R are
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov) gives the primary alcohol P (butan-1-ol); anhydrous CrO$_3$ stops oxidation at the aldehyde stage, giving Q (butanal); CH$_3$MgBr then adds to the aldehyde, and aqueous workup gives the secondary alcohol R.

questions.q: Ethyl alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K. The major product formed is
questions.explanation: At the lower temperature of 413 K, conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ promotes intermolecular dehydration of ethanol to give diethyl ether; dehydration to ethene requires the higher temperature of about 443 K.

questions.q: Phenol can be distinguished from propanol by using the reagent
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give an immediate white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, whereas propanol does not react with bromine water.

questions.q: Match the following with their pKa values: Acid: (I) Phenol (II) p-Nitrophenol (III) Ethyl alcohol (IV) Picric acid; pKa: (a) 16 (b) 0.78 (c) 10 (d) 7.1
options: I - b, II - a, III - d, IV - c
I - c, II - d, III - a, IV - b
I - a, II - d, III - c, IV - b
I - a, II - b, III - c, IV - d
questions.explanation: Ethanol (pKa≈16) is least acidic, phenol (pKa≈10) is more acidic, the electron-withdrawing nitro group makes p-nitrophenol more acidic (pKa≈7.1), and the three nitro groups in picric acid make it strongly acidic (pKa≈0.78): I-c, II-d, III-a, IV-b.

questions.q: CH$_3$-C(CH$_3$)$_2$-OCH$_3$ + HI $\rightarrow$ A + B. A and B respectively are
questions.explanation: Cleavage of this tertiary alkyl methyl ether by HI proceeds via S$_N$1 at the more stable tertiary carbocation, giving tert-butyl iodide and methanol (A = CH$_3$OH, B = tert-butyl iodide).

questions.q: 8.8 g of monohydric alcohol added to ethyl magnesium iodide in ether liberates 2240 cm$^3$ of ethane at STP. This monohydric alcohol when oxidised using pyridinium chlorochromate forms a carbonyl compound that answers silver mirror test (Tollen's test). The monohydric alcohol is
questions.explanation: Moles of ethane = 2240/22400 = 0.1 mol = moles of alcohol, so molar mass = 8.8/0.1 = 88 g/mol, matching 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol, a primary alcohol whose PCC oxidation gives an aldehyde (positive Tollens' test).

questions.q: When a tertiary alcohol 'A' (C$_4$H$_{10}$O) reacts with 20% H$_3$PO$_4$ at 358 K, it gives a compound 'B' (C$_4$H$_8$) as a major product. The IUPAC name of the compound 'B' is
questions.explanation: Acid-catalysed dehydration of tert-butanol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) can give only 2-methylpropene as the alkene product.

questions.q: PCC is
options: A complex of chromium trioxide with pyridine + HCl
questions.explanation: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is the complex formed from chromium trioxide, pyridine and HCl.

questions.q: CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$OH $\xrightarrow{PCC}$ CH$_3$-CH=CH-CHO. Hybridisation change involved at C-1 in the above reaction
questions.explanation: PCC oxidises the primary allylic alcohol to an aldehyde without affecting the double bond; C-1 changes from CH$_2$OH (sp$^3$) to CHO (sp$^2$).

questions.q: A better reagent to oxidize primary alcohols into aldehyde is:
questions.explanation: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidant that stops the oxidation of a primary alcohol at the aldehyde stage, unlike stronger oxidants such as acidified dichromate, which further oxidise it to the carboxylic acid.

questions.q: Compounds P and R in the following reaction are: CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ CH_3MgBr}$ P $\xrightarrow[heat]{conc.\,H_2SO_4}$ Q $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_2O_2,\,OH^-]{(i)\ B_2H_6}$ R
questions.explanation: P is propan-2-ol (from Grignard addition to acetaldehyde), which dehydrates to propene (Q); hydroboration-oxidation of propene gives propan-1-ol (R). Both have the same molecular formula C$_3$H$_8$O with -OH at different positions, so they are position isomers.

questions.q: The heating of phenyl methyl ether with HI produces an aromatic compound A which on treatment with con. HNO$_3$ gives B. A and B respectively are,
questions.explanation: HI cleaves the aryl-O bond of anisole to give phenol (A) and CH$_3$I; nitration of phenol with concentrated HNO$_3$ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, i.e. picric acid (B).

questions.q: Phenol [ring with -OH] is treated with NaOH to give A; A is treated with (i) CO$_2$ (ii) H$^+$ to give B; B is treated with (i) (CH$_3$CO)$_2$O (ii) H$^+$ to give Y (Major product). Y in the above reaction is
questions.explanation: Phenol + NaOH gives sodium phenoxide (A); the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction with CO$_2$/H$^+$ gives salicylic acid (B); acetylation of the phenolic -OH with acetic anhydride gives aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) as the major product.

questions.q: Which is most VISCOUS?
questions.explanation: Glycerol, a triol, has the most extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding among these alcohols, making it the most viscous.

questions.q: The major product obtained when ethanol is heated with excess of conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K is
questions.explanation: Ethanol undergoes acid-catalysed dehydration with excess conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K to give ethene.

questions.q: Among the following, the products formed by the reaction of anisole with HI are :
questions.explanation: With HI, the alkyl-oxygen bond of anisole cleaves by S$_N$2 attack of I$^-$ on the methyl carbon, giving phenol and iodomethane (the stronger aryl C-O bond is not broken).

questions.q: An organic compound with molecular formula C$_7$H$_8$O dissolves in NaOH and gives a characteristic colour with FeCl$_3$. On treatment with bromine, it gives a tribromo derivative C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$. The compound is
questions.explanation: m-Cresol has all three ring positions activated toward electrophilic substitution by -OH (2,4,6-positions) left unblocked by the methyl group (at position 3), so it readily forms a 2,4,6-tribromo derivative; in o- and p-cresol the methyl group blocks one of these positions, allowing only a dibromo product.

questions.q: In Kolbe's reaction the reacting substances are
questions.explanation: In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide (sodium phenate) reacts with CO$_2$ under heat and pressure, and subsequent acidification gives salicylic acid.

questions.q: The major product of the following reaction is CH$_2$ = CH – CH$_2$ – OH $\xrightarrow[Excess]{HBr}$ product
questions.explanation: Excess HBr first substitutes the allylic OH to give allyl bromide, then adds across the double bond (Markovnikov) to give CH$_3$–CHBr–CH$_2$Br.

questions.q: [Cumene] + O$_2$ $\rightarrow$ [cumene hydroperoxide] $\xrightarrow[H_2O]{H^+}$ A+B. The product 'A' gives white precipitate when treated with bromine water. The product 'B' is treated with Barium hydroxide to give the product C. The compound C is heated strongly to form product D. The product D is
questions.explanation: Cumene process gives phenol (A, gives white ppt with bromine water) and acetone (B); base-catalysed aldol condensation of acetone gives diacetone alcohol (C), which on strong heating dehydrates to mesityl oxide, 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (D).

questions.q: A compound 'A' (C$_7$H$_8$O) is insoluble in NaHCO$_3$ solution but dissolve in NaOH and gives a characteristic colour with neutral FeCl$_3$ solution. When treated with Bromine water compound 'A' forms the compound B with the formula C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$. 'A' is
options: Benzyl alcohol: ring with a CH$_2$OH substituent (not phenolic)
m-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on carbons separated by one position (meta)
o-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on adjacent carbons (ortho)
p-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on opposite carbons (para)
questions.explanation: A is soluble in NaOH (phenolic, not carboxylic since insoluble in NaHCO$_3$) and gives colour with FeCl$_3$, so it is a cresol (methylphenol). Only m-cresol leaves all three ring positions activated by -OH (2,4,6) free of the methyl group, so it can brominate at all three to give the tribromo derivative C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$; in o- and p-cresol the methyl group occupies one of these activated positions, allowing only a dibromo product.

questions.q: CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_3O^+]{(i) CH_3MgBr}$ A $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{Conc\ H_2SO_4}$ B $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_2O, OH^-]{(i) B_2H_6}$ C. A and C are
questions.explanation: A is isopropanol (2-propanol) from Grignard addition; dehydration gives propene (B); hydroboration–oxidation of propene (anti-Markovnikov) gives 1-propanol (C). A and C are both C$_3$H$_8$O but differ in OH position, so they are position isomers.

questions.q: Which of the following on heating gives an ether as major product? P: C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br + CH$_3$ONa; Q: C$_6$H$_5$ONa + CH$_3$Br; R: (CH$_3$)$_3$C-Cl + CH$_3$ONa; S: C$_6$H$_5$CH=CHCl + CH$_3$ONa
questions.explanation: P and Q both undergo Williamson ether synthesis (S$_N$2 at an unhindered primary/methyl carbon) to give ethers; R (3° halide) undergoes elimination and S (vinylic halide) resists substitution.

questions.q: The steps involved in the conversion of propan-2-ol to propan-1-ol are in the order
options: dehydration, addition of HBr in presence of peroxide, heating with alc. KOH
dehydration, addition of HBr, heating with aq. KOH
heating with PCl$_5$, heating with alc. KOH, acid catalysed addition of water
heating with PCl$_5$, heating with alc. KOH, hydroboration-oxidation
questions.explanation: PCl$_5$ converts propan-2-ol to 2-chloropropane; alc. KOH eliminates it to propene; hydroboration-oxidation adds water anti-Markovnikov to give propan-1-ol.

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest base?
questions.explanation: Methanol is a weaker acid than water and acetic acid due to the +I effect of the methyl group, so its conjugate base CH$_3$O$^-$ is the strongest base of the four.

questions.q: Which of the following can be used to test the acidic nature of ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is too weak an acid to react with litmus or the carbonates/bicarbonates, but it reacts with reactive sodium metal to liberate H2 gas, confirming its (weak) acidic nature.

questions.q: The intramolecular hydrogen bond is present in
questions.explanation: In o-nitrophenol the -OH and adjacent -NO$_2$ group are close enough to form an intramolecular (chelated) hydrogen bond, unlike the para isomer which forms intermolecular H-bonds.

questions.q: Phenol can be distinguished from ethanol by the reagent
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol instantly, while ethanol does not react this way.

questions.q: When the vapours of tertiary butyl alcohol are passed through heated copper at 573 K, the product formed is
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration (not dehydrogenation) over heated copper, and tert-butyl alcohol gives 2-methylpropene (isobutylene).

questions.q: What is the increasing order of acidic strength among the following ? (i) p-methoxy phenol (ii) p-methyl phenol (iii) p-nitro phenol
questions.explanation: Electron-donating -OCH$_3$ and -CH$_3$ groups decrease acidity (with -OCH$_3$ decreasing it more due to resonance donation), while the electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group increases acidity strongly, giving i < ii < iii.

questions.q: The products X and Z in the following reaction sequence [benzene + CH$_3$-CH=CH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{AlCl_3/ether, Heat}$ X; X $\xrightarrow{O_2/130^\circ C}$ Y $\xrightarrow{H^+/H_2O, Heat}$ phenol + Z] are
questions.explanation: This is the cumene process: benzene + propene gives cumene (X = isopropylbenzene), which is oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide (Y) and then cleaved by acid to phenol and acetone (Z).

questions.q: Which of the following order is true regarding the acidic nature of phenol ?
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group in o-cresol decreases acidity relative to phenol, while the electron-withdrawing nitro group in o-nitrophenol increases it, giving O-cresol < phenol < O-nitrophenol.

questions.q: Which of the following reagent cannot be used to oxidize primary alcohols to aldehydes ?
options: Heating in presence of Cu at 573 K
questions.explanation: Acidic KMnO$_4$ is a strong oxidiser that over-oxidises primary alcohols all the way to carboxylic acids, so it cannot be used to isolate the aldehyde.

questions.q:
The product formed during the following reaction are

CH$_3$–C(CH$_3$)$_2$–O–CH$_3$ + HI → ?  [(CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–CH$_3$, i.e. tert-butyl methyl ether, reacting with HI]
questions.explanation: HI cleaves tert-butyl methyl ether by an SN1 mechanism at the more stable tertiary carbon, giving (CH$_3$)$_3$C–I and CH$_3$OH.

questions.q: In the reaction : Ethanol $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ X $\xrightarrow{\text{alc KOH}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4,\ \text{Room temp.}\ /\ \text{H}_2\text{O},\ \Delta}$ Z, the product Z is,
questions.explanation: X = ethyl chloride, Y = ethene (elimination by alc. KOH); ethene reacts with cold conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at room temperature to give ethyl hydrogen sulphate, CH$_3$CH$_2$OSO$_3$H (as per KEA key; a grace mark was awarded, likely due to the ambiguous double condition printed over the last arrow).

questions.q: Which of the following compound is most acidic ?
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing $-$NO$_2$ group in o-nitrophenol stabilises the phenoxide ion strongly, making it the most acidic among the choices.

questions.q: The reaction which involves dichlorocarbene as an electrophile is,
questions.explanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with CHCl$_3$/NaOH generating electrophilic dichlorocarbene ($:$CCl$_2$), which attacks the phenoxide ring.

questions.q: Ethanol is converted into ethoxy ethane,
options: by heating excess of ethanol with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 140 °C.
by heating Ethanol with excess of conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K.
by treating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at room temperature.
by treating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 273 K.
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether is obtained by heating excess ethanol with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at about 140 °C (Williamson-type dehydration); excess acid at higher temperature instead gives ethene.

questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their acidic strength: i. m-nitrophenol ii. m-cresol iii. phenol iv. m-chlorophenol
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group of m-cresol reduces acidity below phenol; the electron-withdrawing inductive effect of Cl in m-chlorophenol raises acidity above phenol; the strong resonance and inductive electron-withdrawal of the nitro group makes m-nitrophenol the most acidic, giving ii < iii < iv < i.

questions.q: [Phenol reacts with C$_6$H$_5$COCl/base to give X (the Schotten–Baumann reaction acylates the phenolic OH to give phenyl benzoate); X is then nitrated to give Y (major product)] Y is
questions.explanation: Phenol + C$_6$H$_5$COCl/base gives phenyl benzoate (an ester of phenol); the phenoxy ring bears an –O–CO– (ester) group that is a weak o,p-director, so nitration occurs on that ring, para to it, giving C$_6$H$_5$-COO-C$_6$H$_4$-NO$_2$.

questions.q: When CH$_2$=CH-O-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ reacts with one mole of HI, one of the products formed is
questions.explanation: Vinyl ethyl ether undergoes acid-catalysed addition/cleavage with HI via an oxocarbenium intermediate, breaking down to give ethanal (CH$_3$CHO) and ethyl iodide. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: 0.44 g of a monohydric alcohol when added to methylmagnesium iodide in ether liberates at S.T.P., 112 cm$^3$ of methane. With PCC the same alcohol forms a carbonyl compound that answers silver mirror test. The monohydric alcohol is
questions.explanation: Moles CH$_4$ = 112/22400 = 0.005 mol = moles alcohol (1:1 with CH$_3$MgI, active H), so molar mass = 0.44/0.005 = 88 g/mol, matching (CH$_3$)$_3$C-CH$_2$OH (neopentyl alcohol, MW 88); being a primary alcohol, PCC oxidises it to an aldehyde which gives a positive silver mirror (Tollens') test.

questions.q:
CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(CH$_3$)-CHO + CH$_3$MgBr $\xrightarrow{ether}$ 'A' $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ B

The IUPAC name of 'B' is
questions.explanation: 2-Methylbutanal + CH$_3$MgBr adds CH$_3$ to the carbonyl carbon, giving a secondary alcohol CH$_3$-CH(OH)-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$CH$_3$... on renumbering for lowest locants this is named 3-methylbutan-2-ol.

questions.q: Intramolecular Hydrogen bonding is formed in
questions.explanation: In salicylaldehyde, the ortho -OH and -CHO groups form an intramolecular hydrogen bond within the same molecule.

questions.q: Which of the following is strongly acidic ?
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group in p-nitrophenol stabilises the phenoxide ion, making it more acidic than phenol or cresols.

questions.q: An oxygen containing organic compound was found to contain 52% carbon and 13% of hydrogen. Its vapour density is 23. The compound reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen. A functional isomer of this compound is
questions.explanation: Molecular mass $=2\times23=46$; %C and %H give C$_2$H$_6$O, i.e. ethanol (reacts with Na to release H$_2$). Its functional isomer is methoxymethane (dimethyl ether).

questions.q: Power alcohol is a mixture of
options: 80% Petrol + 20% Benzene + Small quantity of Ethanol
80% Petrol + 20% Ethanol + Small quantity of Benzene
80% Ethanol + 20% Benzene + Small quantity of Petrol
50% Petrol + 50% Ethanol + Small quantity of Benzene
questions.explanation: Power alcohol used as a motor fuel is a blend of about 80% petrol, 20% ethanol with a small quantity of benzene added as a co-solvent.

questions.q: Identify 'C' in the following: benzene + CH$_3$-CHCl-CH$_3$ $\xrightarrow[-HCl]{Anhyd\\ AlCl_3}$ A $\xrightarrow[130^\circ C]{O_2}$ B $\xrightarrow[100^\circ C]{dil\\ H_2SO_4}$ Phenol + C
questions.explanation: This is the cumene process: benzene + isopropyl chloride gives cumene (A), which is oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide (B), and acid hydrolysis gives phenol + acetone (C).

questions.q: Out of the given two compounds [A is 4-nitrophenol, with $OH$ and $NO_2$ para to each other; B is 2-nitrophenol, with $OH$ and $NO_2$ ortho to each other], the vapour pressure of B at a particular temperature is ..............
options: higher or lower than A depending on the size of the vessel
questions.explanation: In B (ortho-nitrophenol) intramolecular hydrogen bonding occurs, so it does not associate strongly and has a higher vapour pressure than A (para-nitrophenol), which has intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.q: Identify B and D in the following sequence of reactions: CH$_2$=CH$_2$ treated with conc. $H_2SO_4$ gives A; A on heating with $H_2O$ gives B; B treated with $PBr_3$ gives C; C treated with reagent D regenerates CH$_2$=CH$_2$.
questions.explanation: A is ethyl hydrogen sulphate; B is ethanol (hydrolysis of A); C is bromoethane (B + $PBr_3$); D is alcoholic $KOH$, which eliminates $HBr$ from C to regenerate ethylene.

questions.q: The compound which gives turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature is ..............
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react fastest with Lucas reagent (conc. $HCl$/$ZnCl_2$) via the $S_N1$ mechanism, giving immediate turbidity; 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol) is the tertiary alcohol here.

questions.q:
Out of the below two compounds, the vapour pressure of (B) at a particular temperature is ...............

[(A) = para-nitrophenol: a benzene ring with $-$OH and $-$NO$_2$ groups para to each other; (B) = ortho-nitrophenol: a benzene ring with $-$OH and $-$NO$_2$ groups ortho to each other]
options: higher or lower than (A), depending on the size of the vessel.
questions.explanation: Ortho-nitrophenol (B) has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, reducing intermolecular association, so it is more volatile and has a higher vapour pressure than the para isomer (A), which has intermolecular H-bonding.

questions.q: One mole of an organic compound 'A' with the formula $C_3H_8O$ reacts completely with two moles of $HI$ to form X and Y. When 'Y' is boiled with aqueous alkali forms Z. Z answers the iodoform test. The compound 'A' is ...............
questions.explanation: Methoxyethane (CH$_3$OC$_2$H$_5$) is cleaved by excess HI to CH$_3$I (X) and C$_2$H_5I (Y); Y hydrolysed with alkali gives ethanol (Z), which gives a positive iodoform test.

questions.q: An oxygen containing organic compound upon oxidation forms a carboxylic acid as the only organic product with its molecular mass higher by 14 units. The organic compound is...............
questions.explanation: Oxidation of RCH$_2$OH (primary alcohol) to RCOOH adds one O and removes two H, a net mass increase of +14; oxidation of an aldehyde would only add O (+16).

questions.q: Phenol $\xrightarrow{X}$ forms a tribromo derivative. "X" is ...............
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts readily with bromine water (aqueous Br$_2$) to give the white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, due to the strong activating effect of -OH.

questions.q: Lucas test is associated with
questions.explanation: The Lucas test (ZnCl$_2$/conc. HCl) distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols by the rate of turbidity formation.

questions.q: The best method for the conversion of an alcohol into an alkyl chloride is by treating the alcohol with
options: Dry HCl in the presence of anhydrous ZnCl$_2$
questions.explanation: SOCl$_2$ with pyridine gives clean alkyl chloride with only gaseous SO$_2$ and HCl byproducts, avoiding rearrangement.

questions.q: An organic compound X is oxidised by using acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$. The product obtained reacts with Phenyl hydrazine but does not answer silver mirror test. The possible structure of X is
questions.explanation: A secondary alcohol like (CH$_3$)$_2$CHOH oxidises to a ketone (acetone), which reacts with phenylhydrazine but fails Tollen's (silver mirror) test, unlike aldehydes.
